title: Configurable retention windows and differential hashing for prompts/responses/telemetry
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Implement an engineering-grade retention subsystem that provides per-route and per-tenant configurable retention windows for prompts, responses, request logs, and metrics. Include a differential hashing strategy to enable compact evidence bundles and deterministic partial retention (hash-prefix based coarse deletion) and an export job that can produce attested evidence packages for compliance requests.
background: Customers have asked for more granular control of how long different request artifacts are stored (prompt text, model responses, raw request logs, aggregated metrics). Existing retention is coarse-grained and forces full-item retention or full deletion. Legal/compliance teams require reproducible evidence export with cryptographic hashing for attestation. Product previously scoped policy DSLs; engineering needs to implement runtime enforcement, sampling, and secure export paths.
acceptance_criteria: API: Admin endpoints to set per-tenant and per-route retention windows (in days) for artifacts: prompt_text, response_text, request_log, metrics
Enforcement: Background eviction worker enforces retention windows with <24h accuracy and supports immediate purge via API for legal hold removal
Deterministic partial retention: Implement differential hash-prefix scheme to keep first N-bits stable across versions to allow coarse-grained retention without storing full artifacts
Export: Evidence exporter can assemble a signed tar.gz containing requested artifacts, per-item metadata, and a manifest with cryptographic hashes (SHA-256) and a KMS-signed attestation
Sampling: Support configurable sampling rates per-route (0.1% increments) and a deterministic sampling key to ensure reproducible samples for investigations
Monitoring: Dashboards for eviction rate, export latency, and purge errors; alerts for export failures and retention drift
Security: All exports and purge requests are audited and require RBAC permission; security review completed and approved
proposed_solution: Add retention metadata to request index (retention_policy field with per-artifact TTLs and sampling config). Implement a two-stage eviction pipeline: mark-phase where items are flagged for deletion and export-safe-checks are performed, then sweep-phase where data is removed from primary stores and any KV cache references are dropped. Use deterministic hashing: compute SHA-256 over canonicalized artifact, store only hash prefix (configurable prefix length) when policy requests partial retention. Build evidence-export microservice that queries index, rebuilds artifacts from primary stores (or attaches attestations if retained only as hashes), composes signed manifest, and packages via S3 staging with pre-signed audit trail. Expose Admin REST endpoints: GET /admin/retention/{tenant}, POST /admin/retention/{tenant}, POST /admin/export/{tenant}/evidence.
design_decisions: Index-based enforcement vs per-store TTL: choose index-based mark/sweep to support complex per-artifact policies and exports
Hash-prefix scheme: keep variable prefix length per-tenant to balance privacy vs utility; default 64-bit prefix (16 hex chars)
Sampling: deterministic sampling using HMAC(key=tenant_sampling_key, data=request_id) to ensure reproducibility across jobs
Export signing: use KMS to sign manifest; do not ship raw KMS keys in exports; use ephemeral signing tokens for automation
Immediate-purge contract: admin purge API will call eviction mark-phase and trigger synchronous sweep; heavy purges run as rate-limited background tasks
implementation_tasks: Schema: extend request_index table (or index service) with retention_policy JSON blob and hash_prefix fields
API: implement admin retention endpoints in control-plane service with validation and RBAC checks
Worker: build retention-evictor service as Kubernetes CronJob + on-demand run; implement mark and sweep logic
Hashing: canonicalization library for prompt/response to ensure stable hashes across minor formatting differences
Exporter: implement evidence-export microservice with S3 staging, manifest generator, KMS signing and audit-log write
Sampling: add deterministic sampler util and apply at ingestion path to annotate sampled=true/false
Testing: unit tests for hash determinism, integration tests for end-to-end export, load tests for sweep-phase
Dashboarding: add Grafana panels for eviction throughput, export success rate, purge latencies, and orphaned-hash ratio
Docs: runbook for operations and Confluence page describing retention policy model and legal export steps
risks: Data loss: incorrect mark/sweep could delete artifacts earlier than intended; mitigated by canary runs and dry-run mode
Performance: sweep-phase may impact primary stores under large-scale purge; mitigate with rate-limiting and back-pressure
Hash collisions: truncated prefix may collide and impede investigations; default prefix chosen conservatively and option to increase prefix length
Compliance edge-cases: legal hold semantics must override retention windows and be tested with exports
test_plan: Unit: canonicalization and SHA-256 prefix determinism tests across payload shapes
Integration: ingestion -> retention annotation -> mark/sweep -> verify physical deletion on staging cluster
Export: generate evidence package for sample tenant, verify manifest hashes, KMS signature verification, and audit-log entries
Chaos: run simulated heavy purge while traffic hits runtime to validate back-pressure and no request degradations
E2E: QA flow for immediate-purge API with RBAC denied/allowed scenarios
rollout_plan: 2) Start with internal audit tenants and 2 pilot customers, monitor eviction and export metrics for 2 weeks
3) Gradually open to more tenants and expose admin endpoints to customer success with training
4) Default hash-prefix to conservative size and provide per-tenant override after security review
5) Post-launch: run scheduled audits to compare expected vs actual retention counts
monitoring: audit-log: admin.retention.change events must be captured in SIEM
comments: 2026-03-02 Aisha Khan: initial scoping and trade-offs discussed with PM and Security. Agreed index-based approach over store TTLs to support exports.
2026-03-04 Marco Alvarez: Pushed initial PoC for hash-prefix canonicalization. PR linked above. Needs edge-case tests for user-supplied whitespace and JSON key ordering.
2026-03-06 Security (L. O'Connor): Reviewed approach; requested explicit threat model and KMS key usage policy. Security review added to checklist.
2026-03-09 PM (Jordan Lee): Confirmed compliance acceptance criteria and requested sampling control in Console UI (follow-up PM ticket).
2026-03-11 QA (Mei Chen): Found a race where immediate purge during active export could leave partial artifacts; added gate to block purge while export in progress. Added to implementation tasks.
notes: Keep retention metadata small and index-friendly; avoid embedding large policy blobs per-request. Use policy references and a policy lookup table.
Consider later adding 'redaction pipeline' to transform prompts/responses prior to export when tenant requests PII removal
For on-prem/private deployments, export must be configurable to write to customer-managed S3 or NFS under customer tenancy
